lead: Henderson is one of the newest big cities in the West, but very hard water ages its plumbing fast. Water heater, appliance and slab leaks cause most of its water damage.
risk: hard water damage, water heater failures and flash floods
risk_short: hard water, water heaters, flash floods
why: The median Henderson home was built in 2001, so most pipes are not old. The water is the problem. Las Vegas Valley water is among the hardest in the country, and mineral scale builds up inside water heaters, valves and appliance lines. Tanks fail years early, and fridge and washer hoses crack. Many homes in Green Valley, Anthem and Seven Hills are two-story, so an upstairs leak soaks the ceiling below.

Rain is rare, but summer monsoon storms can be violent. A heavy cell over the McCullough Range sends water rushing through washes and low streets in minutes. Henderson's flood channels carry most of it, but yards, garages and ground floors near washes can still take on water. Monsoon winds also lift roof tiles, and the next storm finds its way in.

tips: Flush the water heater once or twice a year to clear scale.
Install a water softener to protect pipes and appliances.
Replace fridge and washer hoses with braided steel lines.
Keep yard drains clear before monsoon season.
areas: Calls come from Green Valley, Anthem, Seven Hills, MacDonald Ranch, Inspirada, Lake Las Vegas, Whitney Ranch and Black Mountain, plus Boulder City and Las Vegas.

faq.q: Why do water heaters fail so fast in Henderson?
faq.a: Henderson's water is very hard. Minerals settle as scale in the bottom of the tank, which makes it work harder and wears out the lining. Many tanks last only 8 to 10 years here. Flushing the tank and adding a softener help. A drain pan and leak alarm limit damage when one fails.
